identification.title: Son of God
identification.notes: The list's attribution to Sovereign Grace / Worship Initiative is wrong: this is a Starfield song, track 3 on Beauty in the Broken (Sparrow, 16 May 2006) with Chris Tomlin as guest vocalist. Wikipedia's track listing credits Jon and Tim Neufeld; a search summary of WorshipTogether's catalogue also lists Ed Cash and Gordon Cochran, which I did not confirm on the page itself, so the writer credit is uncertain. Publisher and CCLI number were not found. If a different Sovereign Grace song of the same name is intended, this review does not cover it.

claims.structuralNotes: Four short verses, an adoration section and a closing lift of praise, with no distinct chorus. The verses address Christ as creator and as the one who dwells in the heart; as the Father's gift and the sacrificial Lamb; as strength and kindness; and as the promised redeemer, asked to come again. The closing section is praise of his worthiness and beauty. The voice addresses Christ directly, mostly 'You', with personal and corporate pronouns in places. It leans on Colossians 1, John 3:16, 1 Peter 1, Isaiah 7 and 9, and Revelation 5 and 22.

claims.claim: Christ is the creator of all things.
claims.subject: Christ the creator

claims.claim: Christ dwells in the believer's heart.
claims.subject: Indwelling of Christ

claims.claim: Christ is the Father's gift to the world.
claims.subject: The Father's gift

claims.subject: Atonement

claims.subject: Prophecy and return

strengths.title: Christ as creator and Lamb
strengths.explanation: The song joins Christ's work as creator with his work as the sacrificial Lamb, so the one worshipped is both the maker of all things and the one whose blood redeems.
strengths.scriptureRationale: All things created through and for Christ, who holds them together.

strengths.title: The Father's gift, the Lamb's blood
strengths.explanation: Christ is given by the Father and offered as the Lamb, so redemption is traced to the Father's love and Christ's sacrifice, not to the singer.
strengths.scriptureRationale: God so loved the world that he gave his Son.

strengths.title: The promised redeemer and his return
strengths.explanation: The promised Christ of Isaiah is named, and the song closes its story by asking him to come again.
strengths.scriptureRationale: Come, Lord Jesus - the prayer the verse takes up.

strengths.title: Worth as the ground of praise
strengths.explanation: The close praises Christ as worthy and beautiful, so adoration rests on who he is.
strengths.scriptureRationale: The Lamb who was slain is worthy.

doctrinesAffirmed: The incarnation and the Father's gift
Sacrificial atonement by the Lamb's blood
theological.assessment: Nothing to correct. The song speaks of Christ as creator, gift, Lamb, redeemer and returning king, each drawn from Scripture. It names the cross through the Lamb and his blood but does not state sin or substitution plainly. No independent source assessing what it teaches was found.

strengths.title: Short lines, easy to learn
strengths.explanation: Modest repetition and short lines keep the song easy to pick up for a congregation.

strengths.title: Praise that moves through Christ's work
strengths.explanation: The sections move from creator to Lamb to returning king and end in adoration, so a congregation sings an ordered account of who Christ is.

communal.vocalRangeNote: Key not verified; no chart was read. The recording is a band arrangement with a featured guest vocalist, so a leader should set a key in rehearsal.

range.note: No chart was read for this review, so the pitches are not stated.

communal.repetitionAssessment: Repetition is modest. The closing lift repeats praise, but the verses carry the content.
communal.assessment: Congregational in form, with short verses and a simple close, though it comes from a band recording with a featured vocalist. It suits a service on Christ's person and work and adapts easily.

strengths.title: Christ is addressed throughout
strengths.explanation: The song names Christ directly as Son, Lamb and Redeemer, so the addressee is never vague.

clarity.assessment: Clear. Its titles for Christ are biblical and familiar. The gospel is implied through the Lamb and the blood rather than told as a sequence, so a visitor would learn who Christ is more than why he died.

synthesis.summary: A song addressed to Christ as creator, the Father's gift, the sacrificial Lamb, the promised redeemer and the one asked to come again, ending in praise of his worthiness. Each image rests on Scripture. Nothing in it is wrong; sin and substitution are not stated plainly. No independent source assessing its teaching was found.
